title: Noahic-Anchored Royal Houses of England/Britain, France, Burgundy, Savoy, Portugal, Romanov Russia & Germanic Nations

nodes.name: Ancient Germanic Nations (Mascou 1737 & Tacitus): Cimbri & Teutones, Suevi, Alemanni, Saxons, Franks, Vandals (Gaiseric) & Lombards (Alboin)
nodes.era: 3rd c. BCE – 6th c. CE (J.J. Mascou 1737; Tacitus Germania)
nodes.role: Early Germanic Tribal Confederations Rooted in Tuisto / Mannus / Ashkenaz
sources: John Jacob Mascou History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
Tacitus Germania
nodes.notes: Mascou traces the major Germanic confederations from Tacitus's Tuisto and Mannus (linked in universal chronologies to Ashkenaz/Gomer) through the Cimbri & Teutones, Suevi, Alemanni, Saxons, Franks, Vandals (Gaiseric), and Lombards (Alboin).

nodes.name: Kingdom of Burgundy: King Gonderic → King Gundobad (Burgundian Law) → King Sigismund
nodes.era: 5th–6th c. CE (Mascou 1737; Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 14)
nodes.role: Burgundian Royal House of the Rhone & Geneva
sources: John Jacob Mascou History of the Ancient Germans (1737)
Modern Universal History Vol. 14
nodes.notes: Mascou and Modern Universal History Vol. 14 trace the Burgundian kings from Gonderic and Gundobad (codifier of Lex Burgundionum) to St. Sigismund before Frankish absorption and the later Kingdom of Burgundy/Arles.

nodes.name: House of Savoy & Sardinia: Duke Witichind of Saxony (Contemp. of Charlemagne) → Bertold → Hubert of the White Hands → Amadeo → King Victor Amadeus I & II
nodes.era: 8th–18th c. CE (Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 14 pp. 125-140)
nodes.role: Ducal House of Savoy & Royal House of Sardinia
sources: Modern Universal History Vol. 14 pp. 125-140
nodes.notes: Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 14 p. 125 derives the House of Savoy from Saxony's Duke Witichind (contemporary of Charlemagne) via Bertold (who received Savoy from Rodolf of Burgundy) and Hubert with the White Hands (d. c. 1050) to Amadeo and King Victor Amadeus II.

nodes.name: Capetian Kings of France: Hugh Capet (987 CE) → Henry I (+ Anne of Kiev!) → Philip II Augustus → St. Louis IX
nodes.role: Direct Capetian Dynasty Bridging Kievan Rus' & Western Europe
sources: Modern Universal History Vol. 9 (History of France)
nodes.notes: Hugh Capet (crowned 987 CE) founded the Capetian line; King Henry I married Yaroslav the Wise's daughter Anne of Kiev, uniting Rurikid Rus' and France through Philip II Augustus and St. Louis IX.

nodes.name: Valois & Bourbon Kings of France: Philip VI → Francis I → Henry IV of Navarre (Bourbon, 1589) → Louis XIII → Louis XIV
nodes.role: Cadet Capetian Royal Houses of Valois & Bourbon
sources: Modern Universal History Vol. 9 (History of France)
nodes.notes: Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 9 traces the Capetian cadet successions from Philip VI of Valois and Francis I to Henry IV of Navarre (first Bourbon King of France, 1589), Louis XIII, and Louis XIV.

nodes.name: Roman, British & Danish Rulers in Britain (Howell 1685): Julius Caesar → Claudius → King Lucius → King Canute (Cnut)
nodes.role: Roman Imperial Governors, British Kings & Danish Crown in England
sources: William Howell Lives and Reigns of the Monarchs of England (1685)
nodes.notes: Howell (1685) opens the English monarchy with Julius Caesar and Claudius, Christian British king Lucius, the Saxon Heptarchy unified under Egbert and Alfred the Great, and the Danish conquest under Canute (Cnut).

nodes.name: House of Plantagenet (England): Henry II → Richard I Lionheart → King John → Edward I → Edward III → Henry V
sources: William Howell Lives and Reigns of the Monarchs of England (1685)
nodes.notes: Ascending from the Anglo-Norman & Wessex heritage via Empress Matilda, Henry II inaugurated the Plantagenet line leading through Richard I, King John, Edward I, Edward III, and Henry V.

nodes.name: House of Tudor (Welsh-English Royal Union): Owen Tudor → Henry VII (1485) → Henry VIII → Edward VI → Queen Elizabeth I
nodes.role: Tudor Sovereigns Linking Welsh Princes & English Crown
sources: William Howell Lives and Reigns of the Monarchs of England (1685)
nodes.notes: Owen Tudor's grandson Henry VII (uniting Lancaster and York at Bosworth Field, 1485) brought Welsh royal pedigree onto the English throne through Henry VIII, Edward VI, and Elizabeth I.

nodes.name: House of Stuart (Union of Scotland & England): King James VI & I (1603) → Charles I → Charles II → James II
nodes.era: 1603–1688 CE (William Howell 1685; Raleigh 1736 Preface p. ix)
nodes.role: Unified Crown of Great Britain (Scottish Milesian & English Tudor Union)
sources: William Howell Lives and Reigns of the Monarchs of England (1685)
Sir Walter Raleigh History of the World (1736 Preface p. ix)
nodes.notes: Descended both from Scottish Dal Riada (Fergus Mor & Kenneth MacAlpin) and from Henry VII's daughter Margaret Tudor, King James VI of Scotland became James I of Great Britain in 1603 (celebrated in Raleigh's 1736 Preface p. ix), continuing through Charles I, Charles II, and James II.

nodes.name: Foundation of Portugal: Alfonso VI of Castile + Teresa & Count Henry of Burgundy → King Afonso I Henriques (1139, Battle of Ourique)
nodes.role: Burgundian-Capetian Founder of the Kingdom of Portugal
sources: History of Portugal (1661 & 1726)
A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
nodes.notes: Connecting Iberian monarchy (Tubal/Spain -> Castile) with the Capetian House of Burgundy: Count Henry of Burgundy married Alfonso VI's daughter Teresa, and their son Afonso I Henriques won independence at the Battle of Ourique (1139).

nodes.name: House of Aviz & Portuguese Asia: King John I → Prince Henry the Navigator → King Manuel I (Vasco da Gama to India, 1498)
nodes.era: 1385–1580 CE (History of Portugal 1661/1726; The Portuguese Asia)
nodes.role: Aviz Dynasty & Oceanic Sea Route to East Africa & India
sources: History of Portugal (1661 & 1726)
Faria y Sousa The Portuguese Asia
nodes.notes: King John I of Aviz (son-in-law of John of Gaunt / Plantagenet) and Prince Henry the Navigator launched the Atlantic voyages culminating under King Manuel I in Vasco da Gama's 1498 voyage to India.

nodes.name: House of Braganza (Portuguese Restoration): King John IV (1640) → King Afonso VI (1656) → Peter II
sources: History of Portugal (1661 & 1726)
A Compendious Chronicle of the Kingdom of Portugal
nodes.notes: John, Duke of Braganza (descending from Afonso, son of King John I of Aviz), restored Portuguese independence as King John IV in 1640, succeeded by Afonso VI and Peter II.

nodes.name: Grand Princes & Tsars of Muscovy: St. Alexander Nevsky → Ivan III the Great (1480) → Tsar Ivan IV the Terrible
nodes.era: 1221–1584 CE (Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 13: History of Russia)
nodes.role: Rurikid Grand Princes of Vladimir-Moscow & First Tsar of All Russia
sources: Modern Universal History Vol. 13 (History of Russia)
nodes.notes: Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 13 continues the Rurikid lineage from Yaroslav the Wise via St. Alexander Nevsky and Ivan III the Great (who ended Golden Horde tribute at the Ugra in 1480) to Tsar Ivan IV the Terrible.

nodes.name: House of Romanov (Russian Empire): Tsar Michael I Romanov (1613) → Alexis I → Emperor Peter the Great (1682–1725)
nodes.era: 1613–1725 CE (Mod. Univ. Hist. Vol. 13: History of Russia)
sources: Modern Universal History Vol. 13 (History of Russia)
nodes.notes: Connected to the Rurikids through Tsar Ivan IV's marriage to Anastasia Romanovna, the House of Romanov ascended in 1613 under Michael I, continuing via Alexis I to Emperor Peter the Great.
